module_title: Higher Education Reforms, GER Targets, SEDGs & Board Exam Restructuring
introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced DSSSB exams, this level dissects the systemic macro-targets of NEP 2020. It covers Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) metrics, the restructuring of Higher Education (HECI), Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups (SEDGs), and the radical Board Exam changes in NCF-SE 2023.

core_concepts.title: Macro Targets: GER & Public Investment
core_concepts.description:
- School Education GER Target: Achieve **100%** Gross Enrolment Ratio in preschool to secondary level by **2030**.
- Higher Education GER Target: Raise the GER in higher education (including vocational education) from 26.3% (in 2018) to **50% by 2035**.
- Financial Mandate: The Centre and States will work together to increase public investment in the Education sector to reach **6% of GDP** (a reaffirmation of the Kothari Commission target).

core_concepts.title: Equity and Inclusion: SEDGs & SEZs
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 groups all marginalized sections under the umbrella term **SEDGs** (Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups). This includes gender identities, socio-cultural identities (SC/ST/OBC), geographical identities (villages), disabilities, and socio-economic conditions.
- SEZs (Special Education Zones): Regions with significantly large populations from SEDGs will be declared SEZs, where all schemes and policies are implemented to the maximum.
- Gender Inclusion Fund: A special fund to build the nation’s capacity to provide equitable quality education for all girls and transgender students.

core_concepts.title: Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 dismantles UGC, AICTE, and NCTE, replacing them with a single, overarching umbrella body for all higher education (excluding medical and legal education): The **HECI**.
HECI has 4 independent vertical pillars:
1. NHERC (National Higher Education Regulatory Council): For regulation.
2. NAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council): For accreditation.
3. HEGC (Higher Education Grants Council): For funding/grants.
4. GEC (General Education Council): For academic standard setting.

core_concepts.title: NCF-SE 2023: Radical Board Exam Restructuring
core_concepts.description:
To eliminate the high-stakes anxiety of board exams, NCF 2023 proposes:
- Board exams will be offered **at least twice a year**, allowing students to retain their best score.
- Shift to a semester system in the Secondary Stage (Grades 9-12) to reduce the sheer volume of material tested at one time.
- Moving away from evaluating months of rote learning toward offering 'on-demand' board exams in the future, where students take the exam only when they feel ready.

important_entities.name: Academic Bank of Credit (ABC)
important_entities.key_fact: Digitally stores academic credits earned from various recognized Higher Education Institutions.
important_entities.significance: Supports the Multiple Entry and Exit system in higher education. If a student leaves a 4-year degree after 1 year (getting a certificate) or 2 years (diploma), their credits are stored in the ABC. If they return years later, they can resume from where they left off without losing progress.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'HECI will replace all higher education regulatory bodies EXCEPT...?' The answer is **Medical and Legal education**. The Medical Council of India (MCI) and Bar Council of India (BCI) remain independent.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: R A F S (Regulation, Accreditation, Funding, Standards)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: NHERC handles **R**egulation; NAC handles **A**ccreditation; HEGC handles **F**unding; GEC sets **S**tandards.

exam_strategy_tips: For UGC NET: Always remember the exact years for GER targets. 100% GER in Schools = **2030**. 50% GER in Higher Ed = **2035**.
